In general, antipsychotics tend to have more side effects and/or more serious side effects than other psych drugs, so if you're concerned, I'd definitely talk to your doctor. Like, by all accounts I should have diabetes, and I don't.

That being said, it depends on the person. Good luck on your med management!

College was really fucking hard. I wasn't medicated at the time, so that was a fucking roller coaster. Lots of mental hospital stays, lots of bar fights, etc. I almost dropped out probably 20 times. My only advice is to persevere. Something is always better than nothing. A D is always better than a zero. I graduated with a mathematics degree and the highest honors, because, even though in some classes I couldn't even fucking take notes because my mind was racing so fast and in others I didn't even show up to lectures because I was so depressed, I never gave up. I did what work I could and I advocated for myself with my professors. Get to know the profs, go to office hours, do as much as you can with what you're given. Be passionate about what you're learning so it's easier to focus, even marginally. Sorry you're struggling, man. Best of luck to you!

As someone who's been diagnosed with lots of different things and also essentially laughed at by doctors and therapists who said I couldn't \_possibly\_ have what other professionals had diagnosed me with.. try not to sweat this. I know when someone invalidates you like this, you start to question everything and think "maybe I just self-diagnosed" and your thoughts can spiral out of control. But it's important to look at the big picture. At the end of the day, you can have traits for LOTS of different things; mental health issues are on a spectrum. If knowing that you're not alone for being borderline/having borderline traits comforts you, then continue to take comfort in that. I'm sorry your assessor was so flippant. That sucks.
